new_note: *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them. There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Elohim (God), and he is Yahuah (God) our Father for ever.* (Tobit 13:3–4). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Tobit sings this from the land of the captivity, and the instruction is not to hide among the Gentiles but to confess Yahuah (God) in front of them, to declare his greatness in the very places he scattered his children into. Yahusha (Jesus) is sending the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in this same chapter, and he gives them the same charge with a promise attached: confess me before men, and I will confess you before my Father. The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King names them before the Father. The confession Tobit called for and the confession Yahusha (Jesus) rewards are one confession, made by the same scattered people in the same territories.
member_note: Tobit 13:3 — *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.* The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King confesses them before his Father (Matthew 10:32).

new_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Tobit lays out the whole order in one breath: Yahuah (God) scourges his people for their iniquities, has mercy again, and gathers them out of all the nations he scattered them into. The scourge was the scattering. The mercy is the gathering. When Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve, he points them at the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the very people Tobit said would be gathered, and the sending is that mercy beginning to move. The gathering Tobit prayed for as a thing still to come is the mission the King commissions.

new_note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Tobit names who gets gathered and from where: the people Yahuah (God) scourged and scattered, brought back out of all the nations. Ezekiel had said the same, *I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side* (Ezekiel 37:21). When Yahusha (Jesus) says he is not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), he is stating the scope of that gathering, not narrowing his mercy. He said it to the woman of Canaan, and she was not turned away; the sheep hear the Shepherd's voice wherever the scattering has carried them, and the hearing shows who they are. The mission to the lost sheep is the mercy Tobit said would follow the scourge.

new_note: *And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.* (Tobit 14:5). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). Tobit, dying, tells his son there will be two returns, not one. First a return to the land and a temple not like the first, which is the house Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah raised after Babylon, a return of Yahudah (Judah) only. Then, after the time of that age is fulfilled, a return from all places of the captivity, Jerusalem built gloriously and the house of Yahuah (God) built in it for ever, as the prophets spoke. That second return has not happened. Between the two stands the work Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into, and he tells them it will not be finished before the Son of Adam comes. The mission to the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) runs through this age toward the return Tobit saw at the end of it.
member_note: Tobit 14:5 — *afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously.* Two returns, the second still to come; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).

new_note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* (Tobit 14:6). *It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.* (Romans 15:27). Paul is carrying a collection from the assemblies among the Gentiles to the poor saints at Jerusalem, and he calls it a debt: they received spiritual things from Jerusalem, so they owe carnal things back. The Gentiles Paul writes to are, for the most part, the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) living as Gentiles among the nations, the people Tobit said would be gathered home. Tobit saw two things coming: his people gathered home, and the nations turning to fear Yahuah (God) truly and burying their idols, with his own people confessing him and being exalted in the next line. The collection belongs to the first of those. It is the gathering made tangible in one generation: the scattered children of Yashar'el (Israel), who had lived among the idols, sending back to Jerusalem what they owed for the spiritual things that came out of it, the idols left behind and the debt of love paid.
member_note: Tobit 14:6 — *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* The collection for Jerusalem is the turning made tangible, carnal things paid back for spiritual things received (Romans 15:27).
